newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - US Industries to expand in Asia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - US Industries to expand in Asia.

text.p: U.S. Industries Inc (USI) will seek acquisitions or partners in Asia to expand its operations in the region, president John Raos said on Wednesday.
The U.S. consumer and building products giant aimed to expand operations of its jacuzzi, collectible toys and vacuum cleaner businesses in Asia, Raos told Reuters in an interview.
"We are very bullish on Asia. We have companies like Jacuzzi and Rexair vacuum cleaners and have plans over the next few years to expand in this region," Raos said.
He said USI would concentrate its expansion efforts in Southeast Asia.
The company reported a net income of US$133 million for the fiscal year ended September 30 1996 against a net loss of US$89 million the previous year.
USI, America's number one supplier of whirlpool beds, would form a subsidiary of Jacuzzi in Singapore in the near future to attack the Asian market, Raos said.
"We are building a jacuzzi plant in Jurong. We will be signing the lease (for the plant) in January and production is targetted to begin on April or May this year," Raos said.
Initial investment capital for the plant was estimated at Singapore $4-5 million.
Raos said while Europe accounted for US$150 million of the worldwide jacuzzi sales of US$400 million, Asia accounted for only US$10 million. "This shows Asia's potential," Raos said.
There were also plans to build another three to four jacuzzi plants in Asia in Malaysia, Indonesia and China -- over the next three-four years.
Raos declined to give the investment budget for the jacuzzi expansion plans, but he said each 45,000-50,000 square metre plant would costs US$4-5 million in capital expenditure.
USI was also seeking partners or distributors for its Rexair vacuum cleaners, but plans were not yet concrete, he said.
The company, which spent US$12 million to get out of the promotional toys business, remained optimistic in Ertl Toys, one of its U.S. companies, he added.

"We got a very good core business in adult collectibile toys, model kits. That business is very consistent and can make US$13-15 million a year and we think we can grow that business by 10-20 percent a year in sales and profits," Raos said.
Expansion of collectible toys would be through organic growth and acquisitions.
"We are looking for potential acquisitions in Singapore to help us expand the collectible business in South East Asia," Raos said.
USI would list its electronic firm, Jade Technologies Singapore Pte Ltd, on the Stock Excahnge of Singapore in the next couple of weeks, he said.
